method: Exa English and Chinese searches, with a supplementary Japanese written source. Search result slots are not unique pages and are not equivalent to reading. Selected relevant text was fetched live in this run; not every linked video, figure or full long document was inspected.

sources.title: Bevel Modifier — Blender Manual
claims: Bevel is a nondestructive alternative to the edit-mode operation; segments add edge loops.
Angle, weight, and vertex-group limits allow selective bevel placement instead of beveling every edge.
Clamp Overlap limits intersecting bevels. Harden Normals preserves adjacent flat shading while modifying bevel-face normals.
sources.version_caveats: Fetched latest page identifies itself as Blender 5.2 LTS; a search result for the same URL said 5.1. Verify installed Blender and its versioned manual. Attribute names and custom normal behavior are version-sensitive.

sources.title: Smooth By Angle Modifier — Blender Manual
claims: This bundled Geometry Nodes asset sets edge sharpness from neighboring face angles.
The Angle input controls what counts as smooth; Ignore Sharpness can override manually marked sharp edges.
Choose smoothing deliberately; flat shading and edge-angle smoothing are different treatments.
sources.version_caveats: Page identifies as 5.2 LTS. Do not assume old Auto Smooth mesh-property APIs or UI locations. Check available operator/asset in the actual version.

sources.title: Decimate Modifier — Blender Manual
claims: An already economical mesh usually does not benefit from Decimate; dense sculpted or subdivided meshes can.
Collapse progressively merges vertices; ratio is calculated using triangle counts.
Un-Subdivide suits regular subdivision-derived grids. Planar simplifies largely flat forms and offers material, normal, seam, sharp, and UV delimiters.
sources.version_caveats: Page identifies as 5.2 LTS. Its Angle Limit wording appears counterintuitive; do not repeat the higher/lower inequality without runtime verification. Preserve boundaries and inspect the result.

sources.title: Clean Up — Blender Manual
claims: Delete Loose removes disconnected loose geometry. Degenerate Dissolve collapses short connected edges.
Merge by Distance merges nearby selected vertices, with a threshold that can also destroy intentional gaps.
Make Planar Faces and Split Non-Planar Faces address different problems; cleanup must match the defect instead of applying every operation blindly.
sources.version_caveats: Page identifies as 5.2 LTS. Names/options should be checked in installed version; thresholds must be relative to asset dimensions.

sources.title: Mesh Structure — Blender Manual
claims: Triangles are planar; quads are useful for deformation and subdivision.
Flat and smooth shading change how normals are interpreted, without adding silhouette geometry.
Useful edge flow follows contours and deformation; more loops belong where bending needs them.
sources.version_caveats: Page identifies as 5.2 LTS. Custom/free-normal storage and importer claims are version-specific and are not promoted to universal skill rules.

sources.title: Remeshing — Blender Manual
claims: Voxel remeshing is useful for sculpt preparation, messy intersections, and approximate stand-ins.
Automatic remeshing is not a reliable source of final deformation topology.
Use manual retopology when topology must follow animation flow; don't voxel-remesh an otherwise healthy mesh merely to lower its count.
sources.version_caveats: Page identifies as 5.2 LTS. Preserve-attribute and quad-remesh options may differ by release; validate actual functionality.

sources.title: 挤出面 — Blender 手册
claims: Extrusion creates border faces and then transforms the selected region.
Canceling the movement does not remove newly created extrusion geometry, so an aborted transform can leave duplicates.
Use explicit axes and inspect face orientation after extrusion.
sources.version_caveats: Fetched Chinese latest page identifies as 5.2 LTS and includes untranslated English. Search discovered a dev page; fetched latest instead. UI/operator options are version-sensitive.

sources.title: Mirror Modifier — Blender Manual
claims: Mirror uses local axes through the object origin, or the transform of an explicit mirror object.
Clipping constrains seam vertices; Merge joins corresponding vertices within the merge threshold.
A correct mirror plane and seam are necessary; keeping the modifier preserves editability.
sources.version_caveats: Page identifies as 5.2 LTS. Use verified mirror origin/axes and safe scale-aware thresholds; don't confuse adding a modifier with applying it destructively.

sources.title: Low-Poly 3D Assets in Blender Tutorial — Zenva/GameDev Academy
claims: Primitive parameters control segment density at creation time.
Orthographic views, numeric transforms, and snapping support proportion and alignment checks.
Simple forms can be assembled from a small vocabulary of primitives before adding complexity.
sources.version_caveats: Originally 2019; page updated 2024. Old UI, mixed transcript versions, and deliberately customized keyboard shortcuts are not current defaults. No claim of viewing embedded videos.

sources.title: Creating a game sprite: Box Modelling the basic outline — Mike/GameFromScratch
claims: A mirrored primitive can be shaped with extrusion, loop insertion, and vertex adjustments against top and side references.
Adding detail later is easier than removing poorly planned complexity.
Quads and coherent loops improve editability; the final mesh still needs predictable triangulation.
sources.version_caveats: 2013 tutorial. Retain modeling reasoning, not obsolete shortcuts, interface positions, or exact commands; its wording sometimes conflates adding and applying a modifier.

sources.title: Beginner's Overview of 3D Game Asset Creation — Chunck Trafagander/CG Cookie
claims: Use references or a sketch so geometry is not built solely from an untested mental image.
When reducing a high-poly source, prioritize silhouette-affecting detail; excessive reduction can cause bake artifacts.
The appropriate stages depend on the asset; one high-to-low pipeline is not mandatory for all work.
sources.version_caveats: 2024 article; software/product recommendations were not adopted. Post-bake geometry changes are not generalized as safe because triangulation/tangent/bake consistency must be checked.

sources.title: ローポリで素体を作ろう！作るときのコツとは？ — CGbox
claims: Runtime economy and intentionally faceted visual style are distinct meanings of low poly.
Each vertex has strong silhouette impact; keep a distant overall view during modeling.
Add joints and complexity according to actual use; simplify hands and concealed forms when the design permits.
sources.version_caveats: Blender 2.9 tutorial, originally 2021 and updated 2023. Arbitrary ring-count rules and the broad claim that all game meshes are low-poly were rejected; no claim of viewing video.

sources.title: Creating a Low Poly Medieval House in Blender: Part 1
sources.read_status: substantial text read: house, roof, balcony, timber sections; extraction capped at 18,000 chars
claims: Begin from a box, extrude storeys, merge paired top vertices into a roof ridge, then form eaves and roof thickness.
Repeat timber pieces by duplication and rotation; locate the origin at the building base.
Remove faces enclosed inside the building when they cannot be seen and the downstream use permits open geometry.
sources.version_caveats: 2015 tutorial uses Blender 2.7-era right-click selection, Background Images and old shortcuts. Reuse geometric intent only; do not copy UI sequences. Hidden-face removal is conditional, not suitable for every export or use.

sources.title: Create a Low Poly Camaro in Blender: Part 1
claims: Build the side profile first with loops at wheel-arch boundaries, wheel centers, door boundaries and upper arch height; remove wheel-center vertices and shape the arches.
Extrude toward the center, remove center faces and mirror with clipping; repeatedly reconcile side, front and top views.
Keep wheels separate as low-sided cylinders and choose their segment count from the required contour rather than adding radial detail everywhere.
sources.version_caveats: 2014 Blender 2.7-era UI and shortcuts; the tutorial's 14-sided wheels are an example, not a universal budget. Some prose has shortcut inaccuracies.

sources.title: How I made my Shelby GT350R model using Blender
claims: Use a cube at real vehicle dimensions to scale and align orthographic blueprints.
Supplement blueprints with photographs of the same vehicle variant because blueprints alone do not establish all forms.
Create the major connected body surfaces before small trim, wheels and handles; test the asset in the target engine.
sources.version_caveats: 2016 reflective project diary. Its later subdivision/PBR and Unity 5 stages are not a prescription for a faceted low-poly asset.

sources.title: Making Metal Structures
claims: Form an L-shaped angle-iron section from a narrow plane and an extruded edge; add thickness with Solidify.
Assemble repeatable structural units from these bars, then duplicate the units to form larger frames.
Add custom bracing only after the broad structure reads coherently.
sources.version_caveats: 2024 tutorial aimed at metal realism. Only model the L cross-section and wall thickness when the expected view resolves them; a rectangular prism may suffice for distant stylized beams.

sources.title: Behind the Scenes: Dark Fantasy Kit – Part II
sources.kind: first-party asset production breakdown; Dotti Hegedüs
claims: Prototype an entire modular family in rough shapes and flat material colors, and test scale and modular assembly in the engine before detailing.
Use box modeling for primary forms and beveled curves for curved forms; reuse Mirror and Array where repetition is deliberate.
Very small baked ornaments caused repeated cleanup work; the author shifted such detail toward alpha-generated normals.
sources.version_caveats: 2018 high/low PBR workflow. Old Auto Smooth, material packing and engine references need current validation. Microdetail baking is optional for graphic low-poly styles.

sources.title: Procedural low poly trees
claims: Generate a branching edge skeleton by turning new branches relative to the parent direction and shrinking lengths by recursion depth.
Vary branch direction and whether branching occurs; use per-vertex radii with Skin to give the skeleton thickness.
Place low-poly foliage volumes at branch ends rather than modeling individual leaves.
sources.version_caveats: 2022 conceptual implementation. Randomization should be seeded and bounded for repeatable art direction; that restriction is synthesis, not a documented author setting.

sources.title: Complete 3D Game Character Creation Guide (From Blender to Godot)
sources.read_status: read reference setup/head sections and targeted knees, shoulders, elbows/hands sections; did not claim whole 105k-character article reviewed; also hair construction, bangs, main hair, and clothing/shirt sections
claims: Align front/side references to shared body landmarks and real scale; inspect perspective as well as orthographic views.
For an expressive face, establish mouth and eye loops first, add their side-view depth, then connect the surrounding head.
At bending joints, allocate geometry to the outside form and simplify the compressed inside; the tutorial uses inset, knife cuts and edge dissolution.
sources.version_caveats: Written for Blender 4.0+/Godot 4.2+. Subdivision, anime facial detail, addons and toon shading are optional and may conflict with a compact faceted style. Avoid treating its style or vertex counts as universal.

sources.title: Blender—lowpoly风格化案例之进阶篇—林中纸鹤—第三节课：树木、石头模型制作图文教程
sources.read_status: full written lesson read; embedded video not watched
claims: Conifers can combine a low-sided trunk with layered conical crowns, varying each layer in size and outline.
Broadleaf trees can combine several chunky crown masses of different sizes.
The rock example uses a generator followed by decimation. Treat this as a candidate route, not a substitute for deliberate final shape design.
sources.version_caveats: The tutorial explicitly uses Blender 3.2.1; verify add-on availability separately. It describes M as grouping, so confirm the actual command in the installed version. Only page text was read, not the paid video.

sources.title: Optimizing topology for a game Character
sources.read_status: read theory, method, results and partial discussion from first 18,000 extracted chars; figures not visually inspected
claims: The author's controlled comparison found inside knee/elbow collapse with one edge arrangement and better retained form with a different arrangement.
Test topology by posing it; a clean rest-pose mesh is insufficient evidence of deformation quality.
The author identifies weight painting, rig structure, limited body-type coverage and absent extreme shoulder poses as limitations.
sources.version_caveats: 2018 small case study, not a universal anatomical theorem. Do not attribute all deformation errors to topology: joint position, weights and twist bones also matter.

sources.title: Animated Low Poly Characters
sources.kind: original bachelor thesis; Valtteri Iisakki Jolma, 2014
sources.read_status: read introduction, visual style, polycount, topology and initial rig section from 18,000 extracted chars; figures not visually inspected
claims: Cylinder circumference constrains connected body topology; determine limb cross-sections deliberately.
Extra joint geometry can preserve form with a modest triangle cost, while bone pivot placement changes the same mesh's deformation.
The chosen diagonal in a deformed quad can materially change low-poly shoulder appearance; examine final triangulation under pose.
sources.version_caveats: 2014 hardware, texture and bone budgets are obsolete and excluded. Strong claims against subdivision are style-specific, not general modeling rules.

sources.title: Skin Modifier — Blender 5.2 LTS Manual
claims: Skin produces a surface from an edge/vertex skeleton and per-vertex radii; original faces are ignored.
Branch intersections can overlap; Branch Smoothing relaxes them while also shrinking the result.
Skin's Symmetry preserves topology symmetry but does not duplicate geometry; use Mirror above Skin when a mirrored skeleton is required.
sources.version_caveats: Live /latest page identified itself as Blender 5.2 LTS when fetched on 2026-10-16 Asia/Shanghai. Must validate installed Blender version. This is a manual label, not independent release-status evidence.

sources.title: Proportional Editing — Blender 5.2 LTS Manual
claims: Proportional Editing transforms nearby unselected elements with adjustable radius and falloff.
Connected Only follows mesh connectivity, preventing nearby disconnected fingers or pieces from moving together.
Projected from View ignores depth; the manual's landscape example uses a triangulated grid with proportional height edits.
sources.version_caveats: Live /latest page identified itself as Blender 5.2 LTS when fetched on 2026-10-16 Asia/Shanghai. Prefer installed-version documentation before scripting.

sources.title: How to model a low-poly dog in Blender 3.0 on iPad
sources.kind: first-party worked tutorial by tool provider
claims: Shape the abdomen from a half-cube with Mirror, extend neck/head/haunches in side view, then adjust widths from another view.
Extrude legs from belly faces and add loops where contour or joints demand changes; correct their stance from the front.
Ears and tail can be tapered through successive extrusions, with the tip merged after the broad silhouette is correct.
sources.version_caveats: Blender 3.0 and Astropad-specific UI. Several axis/left-right descriptions are inconsistent; preserve geometric construction rather than literal controls. A tiny intentional ear recess should not become an accidental open boundary.

sources.title: Low-Poly Forest Environment – Free Blender Tutorial & File
sources.read_status: overview text read; linked blend/video not inspected
claims: The page describes a scene blockout using a displaced ground plane, cylinder trunks, cone/sphere canopies and scaled icosahedron rocks.
sources.version_caveats: Excluded from core rules: generic counts, mandatory apply-all-modifiers, aggressive UV minimization and small-detail advice lack sufficient context. Do not claim its video or file was studied.

sources.title: Build-a-bird Tutorial
sources.read_status: brief written outline read; videos not watched
claims: The outline starts with cube extrusion blockout and later includes mirroring, rigging and weight-paint troubleshooting.
sources.version_caveats: Not sufficient evidence for detailed topology steps; excluded from core recipes.

sources.title: Building a Stylized Low-poly Modular Diorama for the first time
sources.version_caveats: Not used as evidence.

sources.title: Blender Manual — glTF 2.0
claims: glTF export triangulates quads and n-gons. UV and normal discontinuities can increase exported vertex count.
The exporter recognizes selected Blender material-node arrangements; it does not serialize arbitrary shader graphs.
Export evaluated modifier results and inspect attribute/material settings. Current documentation includes shared accessors.
version_caveats: Page identifies itself as 5.2 LTS; this does not establish release status. Pin documentation to installed Blender.
Alpha-mode detection, node sockets, exporter options, extensions and material-color handling are version-sensitive.

sources.title: Godot — Model export considerations
claims: Godot cameras look toward -Z; oriented models conventionally face +Z. Blender model front maps from -Y.
Control triangulation in the authoring tool before export. Validate transforms and rest pose.
Lighting should be judged in the target engine because engines render it differently.
version_caveats: Fetched stable page identifies Godot 4.7. Verify against project's installed version and conventions.
Do not blindly apply all transforms to an existing rig.

sources.title: Godot — Available 3D formats
claims: Godot recommends glTF; .blend import invokes installed Blender's glTF exporter.
Explicit glTF export removes the Blender installation dependency from consumers; .blend supports rapid local iteration.
Check material culling intentionally. Existing legacy FBX import configuration can persist across Godot upgrades.
version_caveats: Options and requirements are current-page claims, not assumptions for every installed release.
Do not repeat old claims that all FBX import requires external FBX2glTF; newer import paths use ufbx.

sources.title: Godot — Optimizing 3D performance
claims: Costs include culling, transparency, lighting, skinning and draw submission, not just triangles.
Repeated meshes/materials can benefit from instancing. Spatial grouping still matters for culling.
Use LOD and visibility ranges according to the scene rather than universally reducing every mesh.
version_caveats: latest explicitly warns it is unstable. Forward+-specific automatic instancing is renderer-sensitive.

sources.title: Godot — GPU optimization
claims: Reuse materials and shaders; atlas use can reduce texture/state changes.
Combining meshes trades fewer submissions against worse per-object culling.
Measure frame time on target hardware; transparent overlap, fragment work and shadows may dominate a low-poly scene.
version_caveats: latest is unstable. Some broad mobile statements are dated; avoid carrying them into a general rule.
No universal triangle or draw-call budget follows from this page.

sources.title: Godot — Mesh level of detail (LOD)
claims: Imported scene meshes can receive automatic LOD using meshoptimizer; selection is screen-space dependent.
Compare LOD on/off in wireframe and frame-time views; disable problematic meshes or author manual alternatives.
A MultiMesh group shares LOD selection and culling bounds, so geographically distant groups should be separated.
version_caveats: latest is unstable. Default import settings, property names and thresholds must be verified in the target version.
Low-poly faceted assets may need artistic silhouette checks beyond an automatic geometric metric.

sources.title: Godot — Import configuration
claims: Tangents are needed for tangent-space normal/height features; unnecessary attributes can be omitted after confirming material needs.
UV2 lightmap generation is a distinct import setting from surface-color UVs.
Inherited scenes and import settings support repeatable reimport workflows without editing generated resources.
version_caveats: Fetched stable page identifies 4.7; Blender-specific importer options are version-sensitive.
Do not prescribe all import switches globally; branch by actual asset features.

sources.title: Godot — Advanced Import Settings
claims: Use primitive or appropriate convex collision for moving bodies; triangle-mesh collision is for static bodies.
Extracted external materials survive reimport; renaming source materials can break those associations.
Per-mesh LOD/normal-merge settings can resolve specific imported artifacts.
version_caveats: latest is unstable. Verify exact inspector controls and supported physics shapes in the selected engine backend/version.

sources.title: Khronos glTF Tutorial — Meshes
claims: Each mesh primitive connects vertex attributes, optional indices and a material.
An index identifies the complete aligned attribute entry, rather than only a geometric position.
Nodes can share a mesh resource, allowing transform variation without duplicating authored geometry.
version_caveats: This explains glTF 2.0 structure; it is not a guarantee about any engine's batching implementation.

sources.title: Khronos glTF 2.0 Specification
sources.read_status: fetched twice; coordinate, mesh and material sections read
claims: glTF uses meters and a right-handed Y-up system with asset front +Z.
Primitives correspond to GPU draw data; splitting allows material assignments, but final render-pass draw count is engine-dependent.
Base-color textures use sRGB transfer while metallic/roughness and normal data are linear. COLOR_0 multiplies base color.
version_caveats: Retrieved document header identifies specification 2.0.1 dated 2021-10-11. It is authoritative for this snapshot; do not label it the latest revision.
Extensions and renderer behavior require separate verification.

sources.title: 《一厘米时光》开发日志(2) — 调色板
claims: The developer maps model UV regions into a small palette and changes palette colors in Godot.
Palette coordinates can encode semantic color roles for engine-side recoloring.
This is a practical style/pipeline example, not a universal performance benchmark.
version_caveats: Published 2025-06-18. Author explicitly distinguishes their rounded flat-color style from faceted low-poly.
The author's one-material-one-drawcall shorthand is not adopted as an exact invariant.

sources.title: Hubs — Using the Blender glTF Exporter
sources.read_status: fetched and read; version-sensitive recipes excluded
claims: Export troubleshooting should check scale, placement, selected export scope and target-platform material support.
version_caveats: Multiple animation/modifier/unlit recipes describe older exporter behavior. Use only generic diagnostic principles; prefer current Blender manual for implementation.
Hubs-specific Draco and unlit recommendations are not Godot rules.

sources.title: Blender Manual — UV Operators
claims: Choose projection/unwrap methods by shape; Smart UV's lower angle limit generates more islands.
Margin meaning depends on method. Fraction mode relates directly to UV bounds; 1/1024 gives one pixel around an island at 1024 square resolution.
Lightmap layout and surface-paint layout have different requirements.
version_caveats: Fetched page identifies 5.2 LTS. Unwrap methods and labels vary by Blender release.
Do not prescribe a universal 0.008 or 0.01 margin without texture/mipmap requirements.

sources.title: Blender Manual — Triangulate Modifier
claims: Triangulate offers controlled quad diagonals and n-gon tessellation.
An export-copy modifier can lock the diagonal used by the engine while retaining an editable authoring mesh.
version_caveats: Fetched page identifies 5.2 LTS. The page no longer lists the old Keep Normals option; inspect installed RNA/UI rather than assuming old recipes.
